conviction_note: The quarter is pre-released: Q3 was guided to >$186.36M after two September royalty-driven raises, and consensus of $187.0-187.2M sits on that floor. So the print turns on the Q4 guide, the royalty run-rate and licensing after the ITC institution of 2026-10-09. The last pre-raised quarter was sold (-7.05%). The stock is now 34% below its 1 Oct high, and that drawdown coincides with an identified AI-chip sector rout (SOX -13% in 7-8 sessions), not with company news. The findings nearly offset (impact_sum +0.7), so p_up is 51 and abs_move is 18 (median reaction 16.55, about ±22% options-implied, a likely first Q4 guide, beta 2.4).
bar: The revenue bar is Q3 revenue of $187.0-187.2M. MarketBeat has $187.03M and EPS $1.32 (2026-10-13, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-vicor-vicr-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/). Benzinga has $187.1M and EPS $1.27 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VICR/earnings-forecasts). Both agree with the company's 2026-09-30 guide of more than 30% sequential growth, i.e. >$186.358M (https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/vicor-raises-q3fy26-revenue-guidance-30-royalty-boost/52344504). The EPS bar is disputed. Estimates range from $1.27 to $1.39, while stale pre-raise numbers of $0.71 (Earnings Whispers) and $0.99 (ChartRow) are still circulating. There is no company Q4 guide. The standing annual guide is FY2026 revenue >$600M (Q2 call), which a Q4 of about $157M already clears.

OptionsAnalysisSuite's latest settlement is 2026-05-15: 1.6M shares and 1.62 days (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/vicr/short-interest). From the baseline: skew is +8.71 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV 102%, put/call OI 1.02, and the 32-day straddle is 24.25%. Unusual Whales puts the implied earnings move at about ±22% (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/VICR/earnings). The tape is -21.7% over 5 days, -9.3% over 20 days and -46.5% from the 52-week high, with realised vol at 110%. MarketBeat gives beta 2.37, insiders own 28.3% and institutions 47.5% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-vicor-nasdaq-vicr-shares-down-105-time-to-sell-2026-10-15/).

findings.finding: The Q3 number is pre-released, and the last pre-released quarter was sold. Vicor raised Q3 twice: on 2026-09-21 from nearly +10% to >+20% q/q, and on 2026-09-30 to >+30%, i.e. more than $186.358M. Consensus of $187.0-187.2M sits on that floor. In Q2 the company pre-raised its guide, printed $143.35M against a $138.4M consensus with EPS of $1.04 against $0.65, and the stock fell 7.05%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21) beat after a pre-print raise, and the stock fell 7.05% (baseline). Coverage blamed beat quality: royalty income is less predictable than product revenue, opex rose, and Fab-1 is near full utilization (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vicor-beats-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4803455).
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue line is priced, because consensus equals the guided floor. What may be unpriced is the reaction function: a 1-3% beat over a pre-raised number has not paid on this name. If the market expected a big upside surprise, consensus would sit well above $187M. It does not.
findings.independence: The Q2 analog comes from a separate document (the Q2 call transcript) and the baseline's -7.05%. This finding shares the guidance release with finding 2.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the swing line, and its royalty arithmetic cuts both ways. The Q3 raise (≥$28.7M over the ~$157.7M original guide) comes from VPD licence royalties, with licensee, rate and term undisclosed. Recognition could be front-loaded or a catch-up, so Q4 could step down sequentially. The earlier licence, per the Q2 call, steps up from $5M in Q3 to $10M a quarter from Q4 2026 to Q3 2027: a documented +$5M sequential in Q4. The FY >$600M guide needs only about $157M in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 call, the lumpy royalty schedule ($15M in Q2 from termination clauses, then $5M, then $10M) and the CFO saying new licences 'may not result until our second ITC case gets to its final determination in 2027' were cited for the -7.05% reaction despite a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody outside the company knows the VPD royalty's recognition pattern. The 2026-09-16 release gives no rates or term (https://finviz.com/news/392803/vicor-licenses-vpd-to-a-leading-ai-oem). If a Q4 step-down were fully priced, the skew would not need to pay +8.7 points for downside into the print. Net: the known licence is +$5M in Q4, and the VPD piece is unknown in sign and size. The Q4 cliff is an inference from another licence's accounting, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: This finding shares the guidance story with finding 1. The 9/21 CEO comment that four OEMs and hyperscalers hold licences at low early-adopter rates (https://capital.com/en-ae/news/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance) points to recurring but small per-licensee royalties, which is neutral on the sign.

findings.finding: A new licensing lever exists that did not at the last call. On 2026-10-09 the USITC voted to institute an investigation on Vicor's VPD patent. The respondents are Delta, Infineon, Luxshare, Monolithic Power Systems, Flex, Celestica, Quanta, Foxconn and Ingrasys, and Vicor seeks an LEO and cease-and-desist orders. On 9/16 and 9/21 Vicor said early adopters get low royalty rates that escalate, and that four OEMs and hyperscalers are already licensed. The 08:00 ET call is the first place management can quantify licensing interest after institution. In July the guide assumed no new licences until 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Licensing news paid on this name in 2026: +17.7% on the 9/16 VPD licence, double-digit gains on the 9/21 and 9/30 raises, and a gap up on 10/12 on the institution (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-vicor-nasdaq-vicr-shares-gap-up-time-to-buy-2026-10-12/). In Q2 the licensing-timing caveat was blamed for the -7% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The 10/12 gap up has fully reversed. The stock is about $203, against $245 on 10/14 and $217 on 9/17, the day after the first VPD licence and before either raise. The price now gives less credit to licensing than it did before the raises. Against the +8.7 put skew: the skew and the drawdown coincide with a sector-wide AI-chip rout (finding 4), not with Vicor news, so they reflect sector hedging more than a view on the licensing line. That is the reason for filing a positive against the skew, and the size is still kept modest.
findings.independence: The CEO statement on four licensees and low early rates is a separate company release (https://capital.com/en-ae/news/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance). The ITC institution is also on the USITC's own notice (https://www.usitc.gov/press_room/news_release/2026/er1009_69342.htm).

findings.finding: The pre-print drawdown has an identified cause, and it is sector, not company. The SOX fell more than 13% over seven sessions through 10/15, its longest losing streak since 2008, on AI-spending doubts. Cited triggers were an FT report of OpenAI's run-rate near $50B against ~$70B expected, September CPI of 3.7% with 92% odds of another Fed hike, and CXMT memory competition. VICR (beta 2.37) fell 10.5% on 10/15 on volume 80% below average, and it is -21.7% over 5 days with no Vicor-specific news found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of the last 7 prints rose. The one large negative (-23.1%, Apr 2025) did not follow a comparable sector washout in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is in the price by definition. The point is that the stock now sits below its pre-raise level on sector beta, while the company-level numbers were raised twice. A print that confirms the run-rate faces a lower bar than the 10/1 price implied. The sector direction over the window is unknowable, and macro-to-company transmission is a proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The KuCoin/BeInCrypto piece of 2026-10-16 has the same SOX streak and causes (https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/chip-stocks-fall-for-8-straight-days-amid-ai-spending-doubts). MarketBeat 10/15 shows the VICR move on thin volume with no cause.

findings.finding: AI-infrastructure counterparties are still printing strong. TSMC reported Q3 profit up 68.7% in mid-October, after Vicor last spoke, though its US shares fell 1.8% on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Advanced products grew 45% q/q in Q2 (to $94.2M), and the stock still fell 7%. Demand strength has not been the line this name trades on lately.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a broad proxy, and Vicor's product revenue is capacity-limited by Fab-1, so demand strength may not convert into Q3/Q4 product upside beyond the guide. It mostly counters the AI-spending-doubt narrative behind the sector rout.
findings.independence: This shares a document with finding 4. Finding 6 (Cerebras) is a separate demand signal.

findings.finding: Cerebras, which analysts on Vicor's Q2 call asked about as a possible 10% customer (management declined to say), has spoken since Vicor last did. On 2026-08-12 it reported Q2 core revenue of $209.9M (+103%), guided Q3 to $214-216M and FY to $880-890M, and said it plans to increase manufacturing capacity more than tenfold this year. Its RPO is $25.4B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Advanced products grew 45% q/q in Q2 without a positive reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty print after Vicor's last call, but it is a proxy. Vicor has not confirmed Cerebras as a customer in a document I read, and its product revenue is capacity-constrained. The Cerebras print was public for two months, so any read-through is largely in Vicor's own raised guide.
findings.independence: On the Q2 call Vicor declined to say whether Cerebras was a 10% customer (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vicor-beats-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4803455). That shares the transcript with finding 2.

findings.finding: The CEO sold at the top. Patrizio Vinciarelli sold 20,000 shares at $316.13 on 2026-10-01, the day after the second guidance raise. That is 0.24% of his holding. Insiders sold 27,053 shares (~$7.75M) in 90 days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no observable reaction history on insider sales for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: This is public, small relative to his 28%-insider-owned holding, and largely priced. It is filed because selling the day after a raise is a weak tell on management's view of the royalty run-rate.
findings.independence: None from a different source. The Form 4s are on EDGAR (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000751978.json), which is the same fact.

findings.finding: Vicor holds an unused $150M buyback. The board authorised it on 2026-08-25 with no expiry, replacing the prior programme. Cash was about $454M at 6/30 per the Q2 10-Q. With the stock 34% off its 10/1 close, the release or call may disclose repurchases in the quarter or announce intent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed. Buybacks have not been a disclosed driver of past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public, but its use is not. Fab-2/3 capex (finding 9) competes for the same cash.

findings.finding: Vicor is building out capacity. On 2026-09-11 it announced the purchase of a 334,000 sq ft building on 66 acres in Merrimack, NH, and 54 acres in Hooksett, NH, for ChiP Fab-2 and Fab-3 (about 1M sq ft in total). Fab-1 is approaching capacity, and Fab-2 is about a year from running. The call may give the capex for these, with Q2 backlog of $379.7M (+26% q/q) as the demand rationale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The fab announcement itself bought about +11% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/vicor-stock-jumps-new-fab-manufacturing-facilities). In Q2, analysts pressed on capacity limits and the stock fell 7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sites are public, but the capex size and phasing are not. Capex that funds visible backlog is a zero-to-positive, so it is signed slightly positive after asking what the money buys.
findings.independence: The Q2 transcript gave the site down-select and a 2-3x Fab-1 sizing (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vicor-beats-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4803455).

findings.finding: The sell side is bullish with targets far above spot. MarketBeat consensus is Buy with an average target of $391.67 (1 Strong Buy, 3 Buy, 1 Hold). Needham raised its target to $350 on 10/1, Roth reiterated $375 on 9/22, and Zacks upgraded to Strong Buy on 10/1. Spot is about $203.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bullish coverage did not stop the -7.05% reaction in Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and priced. It is filed so the panel sees that the expectation gap is between price and targets, not between consensus and guide. A 2-5 analyst name can see quick target cuts after a soft Q4 guide.
findings.independence: This shares a document with finding 7.

outside_window.finding: The ITC 337-TA-1526 final determination and any Limited Exclusion Order on VPD modules. That is when Vicor says royalty escalation bites most, and it falls far after the window (management spoke of 2027 for the prior case).
The two-year all-inclusive licences must be renegotiated as usage evolves (Q2 call).

baseline_tension: The pre-released-quarter and Q4-royalty negatives agree with the +8.7 put skew. The licensing lever, and the stock trading below its pre-raise level on an identified sector rout, cut against the skew and the -21.7% 5-day run-up. The two sets nearly offset, so p_up is 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (a sign against a strong skew): the ITC/licensing finding went from +1.5 to +1.2, with an explicit reason the +8.7 skew may be sector hedging. p_up went from 52 to 51.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission and proxies): sector rout +0.5 to +0.3, TSMC read-through +0.2 to +0.1, Cerebras read-through +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the Q4 royalty finding went from -0.5 to -0.3, because its own text documents a +$5M Q4 step-up on the earlier licence against an undocumented VPD cliff.
Rules 1 and 6 left the pre-released-quarter finding at -1.0 and print_vs_bar at +1.5. The revenue bar is sourced to the guide plus two agreeing estimates; the EPS bar is flagged as disputed.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (1.4-1.6 days, not crowded), so no change. Rule 8: abs_move kept at 18, above the 16.55 median.
